target_customer: Consumers of African, Afro-Caribbean and African-American film and series, first in France and francophone Africa, paying a monthly subscription
problem: Mainstream streaming services showed little African and Afro-diaspora content. Afrostream licensed that catalogue into one subscription service, with subtitled and dubbed titles.
business_model: SVOD subscription (EUR 7 per month at launch) plus telecom distribution deals

founders.name: Tonjé Bakang
founders.background_notes: Founder letter says the project began in November 2013 and was self-funded at first. YC launch post calls her co-founder and CEO.

founders.name: Ludovic Bostral
prior_employers: M6 (R&D manager on M6 Replay, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page with a streaming technology bio. The founder letter mentions only an unnamed co-founder; timing of his earlier roles relative to Afrostream is not stated.

exit.reason: Investors would not fund a business that was not yet profitable, one investor withdrew in March 2017, buyer talks failed and cash ran out by August 2017.

competitors.name: iROKOtv
competitors.traction_then: described as the dominant African online film player since its 2011 launch

competitors.name: ShowMax
competitors.what: Naspers OTT video on demand service for South Africa
competitors.traction_then: announced in 2015, per a 2015 analysis quoted in search results

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a multi-device streaming app with subtitling, dubbing workflows and telecom set-top integration needed real video engineering from a very small team, but the components were available commercially.

defensibility.rationale: Content licences were non-exclusive and the founder reports subscribers consumed the catalogue within about three months. Larger streamers could license the same titles.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A 2015 AFP piece warned Netflix could outspend the African start-ups on content. No source shows a direct copy. The service shut down in September 2017 after failing to raise a further round.

market_need_then: The YC launch post (July 2015) reports about 2,000 sign-ups and $100,000 in subscriptions within weeks of announcing, and the founder letter says the service passed 10,000 subscribers in April 2016. The company targeted 15 million people of African descent in Europe and large African audiences.

branding.domain_note: Used the .tv domain afrostream.tv per the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as the place for Black and African role models on screen; the YC launch post quotes the founder on looking for role models on TV.

branding.brand_signature: Afrostream Life articles portal and The Tchip podcast extended the brand beyond streaming, per the founder letter.
branding.community_and_virality: A pre-subscription campaign sold about 2,000 annual subscriptions and Orange, Bouygues Telecom and TF1 distribution carried the brand, per the founder letter.

brand_strength.rationale: The descriptive name told customers exactly what the service was and drew trade press in French and English plus telecom partners. No source shows a mascot, merch or viral community, and the brand did not save the business.

outcome_analysis: Afrostream launched on 1 September 2015 after YC and raised roughly $4M including Orange, reaching 10,000 subscribers by April 2016. High content costs and a catalogue that loyal subscribers finished in about three months meant it was not profitable. A 2016 plan to raise $10M went unfunded, an investor withdrew in March 2017, buyer talks failed, cash ran out in August 2017 and subscriptions stopped on 13 September 2017.
notes: Company website afrostream.tv could not be fetched in this session (network allowlist). The founder letter states about $4M raised over two years plus $120K from YC and does not say whether the $4M includes YC; the October 2015 round amount was undisclosed in press, so the $4M is not attached to a round and rounds are partial. One aggregator claims a $12M seed, contradicted by press and the founder letter, so it is not recorded. CB Insights shows $120K over four rounds, also conflicting. The iROKOtv competitor entry rests on a search snippet of the TechCrunch-linked TechCabal article (the page itself returned 403) and the ShowMax entry on a search snippet of an AFP piece. The YC page lists an apparently later bio for the CEO.
